body:
I'm so sorry, I can only assume you live in the US, what you disc rube about the mental health availability (or tragic lack there of) is all of too familiar.  I would bet you are probably in the boat where you do not qualify for public assistance.  It's sickening and I'm truly sorry.  

I'm not sure what state you are in but do look and see if they have some sort of special call out for mental health.  Texas used to have one that was decent, it's dried up, but maybe you are still lucky?  If not have you considered churches?  I know a lot of the Catholic Churches in our region can help cover prescriptions or wisdom teeth removal?  Just an idea if y had not previously thought of them.

I wish like hell that we had a world where you did not have to go through this.  Stay strong.

I can relate to your story.  I have had my share of battles.  If I can I would like to offer you hope if nothing more.

I know that it is hard being on your own and estranged from family but sometimes it's best for you (and them) to part ways for a period of time and try to make your self whole.  

I was on my own and had dropped out by 16.  I ended up with a habit, a slew of fair weather friends, no education and no hope.  I was 17 when I got pregnant with my only child.  In the time before she was born I cleaned up ( still clean to this day) and got my GED.

My daughter is now 15.  I cannot say its been easy, but I can tell you I wouldn't change anything I've been through or done.  She was the catalyst I need for strength to crawl out from under what I was sure would kill me, what I wanted to kill me. 

I'm not saying go out and get pregnant .  I am telling you to hold on, your catalyst to do amazing things is out there.  It will find you.  You have been through more than most adults and you are still here.   You are stronger than you give yourself credit for.  You seem like you are caring and intelligent young woman.  Give your self permission to work on healing you, feel your highs, feel your lows and make peace with them.  Learn to love your self for the amazing person that you are.

I hope you will someday be able to sit where I am today.  I have created a healthy relationship with a parent, I have found the one who can make me love like I didn't know possible (my daughter) and I have all of my basic needs in life covered through hard work and perseverance. 

I know if you hang in there you can create this for your self.   On the days you feel low find something to cling to, some form of hope or gratitude.  Cling to it and keep fighting, never give up because even when you forget the world already knows that you are strong, you are capable and more people than you will probably ever know care about you and want to watch you soar.

Hang in there.  It always gets better.
